either '''Juan Carlos Navarro''' or '''J. C. Navarro''' (born June 13, 1980), is a Spanish former professional [[basketball]] player and current basketball executive. He currently a club ambassador and player mentor of the Spanish [[EuroLeague]] club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet]]. During his playing career, at a height of {{height|ft=6|in=4}} tall,{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/euroleague/players/|title=Euroleague Basketball|website=Euroleague Basketball}}{{Dead link|date=December 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}{{Cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2011.roundID_7526.playerID_27036.teamID_362.html|title=JUAN CARLOS NAVARRO SPAIN Height 1.92m.}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.acb.com/jugador/temporada-a-temporada/id/20200515/tipo_id/1/competicion_id/1/fase_id/0|title=acb.com|website=www.acb.com}} he played at the [[shooting guard]] position. During his playing days, Navarro was nicknamed "La Bomba" ([[English language|English]]: "The Bomb"), which is also the [[Spanish language|Spanish]] name for his signature basketball move, the [[Basketball moves#Tear drop|tear drop]], which was the shot Navarro was a specialist in and became well-known for. Navarro is widely regarded as one of the best European basketball players of all time. Navarro was the [[Eurobasket News All-Europe Player of the Year]] in 2009, 2010, and 2011. He was also named [[Mr. Europa]] in 2010. On March 14, 2014, Navarro was inducted into the Euroleague's Hall of Fame, after he was named a [[EuroLeague Basketball Legend|EuroLeague Legend]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/euroleague/game-center/|title=Game Center | EuroLeague|date=October 17, 2023|website=Euroleague Basketball}}{{Dead link|date=December 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} In 2018, he was named to the 101 Greats of European Basketball selection. Along with the Greek player [[Vassilis Spanoulis]], Navarro was one of just two players, that were still active players at the time, that were specially selected for the honor. All of the other players that were chosen for the honor, had already retired from actively playing. During his pro [[sports club|club]] career, Navarro was a two-time [[EuroLeague]] champion, in [[2003 EuroLeague Final Four|2003]] and [[2010 EuroLeague Final Four|2010]]. He was also named the [[EuroLeague MVP]] in [[2008–09 Euroleague|2009]], the [[EuroLeague Final Four MVP]] in 2010, and he was also selected as a member of the [[EuroLeague 2000–2010 All-Decade Team]] and the [[EuroLeague 2010–2020 All-Decade Team]]. As the [[Captain (sports)|captain]] of the senior [[Spain national basketball team|national team of Spain]], Navarro notably won, among other medals, a [[FIBA Basketball World Cup|FIBA World Cup]] gold medal in [[2006 FIBA World Championship|2006]], two [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|FIBA Summer Olympics]] silver medals in [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008]] and [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012]], as well as two [[FIBA EuroBasket]] gold medals in [[2009 EuroBasket|2009]] and [[2011 EuroBasket|2011]]. He also earned two [[FIBA EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-EuroBasket Team]] selections ([[2005 EuroBasket|2005]], 2011), and was [[FIBA EuroBasket MVP|the competition's MVP]] in 2011. ==Early life== Juan Carlos Navarro Feijoo was born in [[Sant Feliu de Llobregat]], [[Province of Barcelona|Barcelona]], Spain. Navarro began playing [[youth system]] club basketball, with a local club in Sant Feliu de Llobregat, called Club Bàsquet Santfeliuenc, at the age of 8. At the age of 12, he moved to the youth clubs of FC Barcelona. ==Professional career== === FC Barcelona (1997–2008) === Navarro started playing with the senior men's club of [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] at the age of 17, making his [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]] debut on November 23, 1997. That year he was selected to attend the [[Nike Hoop Summit]], but he opted stayed in Europe, and play for the Barcelona pro team. Due to his club obligations, he was also not on the Spanish junior national team that won the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]], in [[Mannheim]], in 1998. With the acquisitions of [[Dejan Bodiroga]] and [[Gregor Fučka]] in 2003, FC Barcelona won all the competitions they played in that year. It was the first time the club won the [[EuroLeague]] championship. By winning the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]], the [[Copa del Rey de Baloncesto|Spanish King's Cup]], and the [[2003 EuroLeague Final Four|2002–03 EuroLeague]] all in the same year, Barcelona won the coveted [[European Basketball Triple Crown|Triple Crown]] championship that year. With Barcelona, Navarro played on [[Liga ACB]] (Spanish League) championship teams eight times: 1999, 2001, 2003, 2004, 2009, 2011, 2012 and 2014; the [[Spanish Basketball King's Cup|Spanish King's Cup]] winners seven times: 2001, 2003, 2007, 2010, 2011, 2013 and 2018; the [[Spanish Basketball Supercup|Spanish Supercup]] winners five times: 2004, 2009, 2010, 2011 and 2015; the [[FIBA Korać Cup]] champions once: 1999; and the [[EuroLeague]] champions twice: [[2003 EuroLeague Final Four|2003]] and [[2010 EuroLeague Final Four|2010]]. Navarro helped Barcelona reach the [[EuroLeague Final Four]] seven times: [[2000 EuroLeague Final Four|2000]], [[2003 EuroLeague Final Four|2003]], [[2006 EuroLeague Final Four|2006]], [[2009 EuroLeague Final Four|2009]], [[2010 EuroLeague Final Four|2010]], [[2012 EuroLeague Final Four|2012]], and [[2014 EuroLeague Final Four|2014]]. Navarro was selected to the [[All-EuroLeague Team]] seven times: 2006, 2007, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2013. In 2006, Juan Carlos Navarro earned the [[ACB Most Valuable Player Award|regular season Most Valuable Player award of the Spanish Liga ACB]]. He was named the [[ACB Finals Most Valuable Player Award|Spanish Liga ACB Finals Most Valuable Player]] in 2009 and 2011. He was named the [[EuroLeague MVP]] in 2009, and the [[EuroLeague Final Four MVP]] in 2010 As a member of [[FC Barcelona Basket|FC Barcelona]], Navarro played with players like [[Sasha Đjorđjević]], [[Artūras Karnišovas]], [[Rony Seikaly]], [[Pau Gasol]], and [[Šarūnas Jasikevičius]], which helped make him a better player, and he became one of the most promising young European players, early on in his career with Barcelona. Several NBA [[mock draft]]s started to set him as a projected [[NBA draft]] pick.{{citation needed|date=September 2019}} In the 2001–02 season, Navarro was plagued by injuries, which dropped his [[NBA draft]] stock. Eventually, the [[Washington Wizards]] drafted Navarro in the second round (with the 40th pick overall) of the [[2002 NBA draft]]. Navarro subsequently declined the Wizards contract offer, as he preferred to stay with Barcelona. On August 3, 2007, the Washington Wizards traded Navarro's draft rights to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for a future first-round draft pick. Navarro would later be reunited with his former Barcelona and Spain national teammate [[Pau Gasol]] on the Grizzlies.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130122210401/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/web/castellano/noticies/basquet/temporada07-08/08/n070803101458.html|title=Navarro alcanza un acuerdo con los Memphis Grizzlies.}} {{in lang|es}} After securing his €10 million contract buyout with Barcelona, Navarro signed a one-year contract with the Memphis Grizzlies of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], and he played with them during the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]]. In his rookie NBA season, Navarro was one of the Grizzlies' team leaders in three-point shooting (.361). He was also named to the 2007–08 [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] after averaging 10.9 points per game. On June 18, 2008, he decided to leave the NBA and return to Spain. He signed a four-year deal worth €12 million [[net income]] (with an optional fifth year that would bring the total contract to €15 million net income) with Barcelona, his former team. A qualifying contract offer, that had been previously tendered to Navarro by the Memphis Grizzlies, was eventually rescinded by the team on September 10, 2009. That allowed the Grizzlies the cap space to then sign [[Allen Iverson]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4462209|title=Grizzlies welcome Iverson with standing ovation|date=September 10, 2009|website=ESPN.com}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbgglobal.eu/nba-basketball/the-grizzlies-give-up-navarro-for-iverson/|title=The Grizzlies give up Navarro for Iverson|date=November 30, 2010}} Navarro's final NBA game was played on April 16, 2008, in a 111–120 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]] where he recorded 16 points, 7 assists, 4 rebounds and 2 steals. === FC Barcelona (2008–2018) === [[File:JCNavarro3.jpg|thumb|upright=1.18|right|Navarro with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]], getting past [[Joventut de Badalona|Joventut's]] [[Pau Ribas]], after a screen performed by [[Daniel Santiago]] (2009).]] [[File:FCBQ) - 41863058261.jpg|thumb|right|Navarro with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] (2017).]] After spending the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]] in the [[NBA]], with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], Navarro returned to [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] in the summer of 2008, on a 4-year [[Euro|€]]12 million [[net income]] contract. The contract included a €10 million buyout amount. The contract also included an optional fifth year, which brought the total contract to €15 million net income. In 2012, Barcelona picked up the fifth optional year of his contract (€3 million net income), and extended him for another two additional years, at a salary of €2.6 million per season after that, bringing the total to €8.2 million net income over three years.{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/89971/180/fc-barcelona-regal-extends-navarro-through-2015 |title=FC Barcelona Regal extends Navarro through 2015 |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=November 21, 2011 |access-date=2012-08-20}} Over the 2014–15 season, Navarro experienced several injury problems with his right leg. In late December 2014, it was announced that he would miss up to six weeks of action, due to a torn muscle in his right thigh.{{cite news|title=FC Barcelona's Juan Carlos Navarro will miss six weeks of action|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/145946/fc-barcelona-s-juan-carlos-navarro-will-miss-six-weeks-of-action.html|access-date=18 July 2015|work=sportando.com|date=23 December 2014}} On June 29, 2015, it was announced by Barcelona that Navarro would miss three months of game action, due to [[plantar fasciitis]] on his right foot.{{cite news|title=Juan Carlos Navarro, baixa esportiva durant tres mesos|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/basquet/basquet-equip/detall/noticia/juan-carlos-navarro-baixa-esportiva-durant-tres-mesos|access-date=18 July 2015|work=fcbarcelona.cat|date=29 June 2015|language=es}} Those injuries negatively impacted his performances over the season, in which he had averages of 10.5 points and 3.1 assists per game, on 37% shooting from the field overall, in 17 [[2014–15 Euroleague|EuroLeague 2014–15 season]] games. On August 17, 2018, Navarro retired from competing in active sports competition,{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/726370/end-of-an-era-juan-carlos-navarro-retired/|title=End of an era: Juan Carlos Navarro retired|date=August 17, 2018|website=Eurohoops}}[https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/juan-carlos-navarro-retires/ar-BBM4e9U Juan Carlos Navarro retires.]{{Cite web|url=https://www.bulletsforever.com/2018/8/17/17715126/juan-carlos-navarro-retirement-washington-wizards|title=Former Wizards draft pick Juan Carlos Navarro announces retirement|first=B. F.|last=Staff|date=August 17, 2018|website=Bullets Forever}} and he joined the FC Barcelona club's head office structure. That fulfilled what had been previously established in the 10-year contract that he signed with the club in September 2017 - that he would join the club's front office, after he retired from playing basketball with the team.{{cite news |title=Juan Carlos Navarro signs agreement to stay at Barça Lassa {{!}} FC Barcelona |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/sections/basketball/first-team/news/2017-2018/juan-carlos-navarro-signs-agreement-to-stay-at-barca-lassa |access-date=17 August 2018 |work=FC Barcelona |date=19 September 2017}}{{cite news |title=Juan Carlos Navarro to join FC Barcelona Basketball structure {{!}} FC Barcelona |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/sections/basketball/first-team/news/2018-2019/juan-carlos-navarro-to-join-fc-barcelona-basketball-structure |access-date=17 August 2018 |work=FC Barcelona |date=17 August 2018}} At the time of his retirement from playing professional basketball, Navarro was the [[EuroLeague]]'s all-time career leader in total [[Performance Index Rating|Performance Index Rating (PIR)]] (that record was eventually broken by [[Vassilis Spanoulis]]),{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/euroleague/news/|title=Latest News | EuroLeague|date=October 16, 2023|website=Euroleague Basketball}}{{Dead link|date=December 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} and also the league's career leader in total points scored (4,152 points) in the modern [[EuroLeague Basketball]] era of the competition, since the year [[2000–01 Euroleague|2000]] (that record was also eventually broken by [[Vassilis Spanoulis|Spanoulis]]). Navarro also retired as the all-time career leader in total [[point (basketball)|points]] scored (4,321 points), in the entire history of the EuroLeague (since [[1958 FIBA European Champions Cup|1958]]), including when the competition was run by [[FIBA Europe]], as he also scored 169 total points in the [[1999–00 FIBA EuroLeague|FIBA EuroLeague 1999–00 season]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_,Uz02qBnJiADOq5VntEf53.season_2000.roundID_2571.playerID_27036.teamID_1030.html|title=JUAN CARLOS NAVARRO FC BARCELONA 1999–00 AVERAGE.}} In March 2019, Navarro's number 11 jersey was [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet#Retired numbers|retired by the club]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/837338/juan-carlos-navarro-jersey-retirement-ceremony/|title=Juan Carlos Navarro jersey retirement ceremony|date=March 1, 2019|website=Eurohoops}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.talkbasket.net/38601-barcelona-retired-juan-carlos-navarros-jersey|title=Barcelona retired Juan Carlos Navarro's jersey|first=Yiannis|last=Bouranis|date=March 1, 2019|website=TalkBasket.net}} ==National team career== [[File:Macedonia against Spain 2.jpg|thumb|right|Navarro with [[Spain national basketball team|Spain's national team]], attacking the paint against [[Macedonia national basketball team|Macedonia]], in 2011.]] In the summer of 1998, Navarro was a member of the [[Spain national under-18 basketball team|Spanish under-18 junior national team]] that won the gold medal at the [[1998 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. He was also one of "The Golden Generation" boys of Spain (along with [[Felipe Reyes]] and future [[NBA]] players [[Pau Gasol]] and [[Raül López (basketball)|Raúl López]]) that defeated the United States' junior national team at the [[1999 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]. Navarro played with the senior [[Spain national basketball team|Spanish national team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2000 Sydney Summer Olympics]]. He also played at the [[2001 EuroBasket]], where he won two games during the tournament with [[buzzer-beater]]s. He scored 27 points during the bronze medal game against [[Germany national basketball team|Germany]]. At the [[2003 EuroBasket]] in Sweden, Navarro won a silver medal with the Spain's national team. In Spain's seventh-place finish at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Athens Summer Olympics]], he scored 18 points in Spain's loss against [[United States men's national basketball team|Team USA]]. At the [[2005 EuroBasket]], the [[Spain national basketball team|Spanish national team]], playing without [[Pau Gasol]], finished in fourth place. Navarro was the second leading scorer of the tournament, with an average of 25.2 points per game, finishing behind only [[Dirk Nowitzki]]. In August 2006, he played on the Spanish national team that won the gold medal at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]], after they defeated [[Greece national basketball team|Greece]] in the tournament's final; after the Greeks had earlier defeated Team USA, in their semifinal, by a score of 101–95. In September 2007, Navarro and Spain lost against [[Russia national basketball team|Russia]], in the gold medal game at the [[2007 EuroBasket]], which was held in [[Madrid]], on Spain's home floor. Navarro was a member of Spain's national team that won the silver medal at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Beijing Summer Olympics]]. Navarro scored 18 points in the gold medal game that Spain lost against [[United States men's national basketball team|Team USA]]. Navarro was part of the Spain's national team that won the [[2009 EuroBasket]]. As the defending champions, Spain retained their European crown at the [[2011 EuroBasket]]. Navarro led his team with a game-high 27 points in the championship game [[EuroBasket 2011 Final|over France]]. He earned [[FIBA EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]] accolades, along with his teammate, [[Pau Gasol]], and he was named the [[EuroBasket MVP]].{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket2011.com/en/coid_0R3VWYPmGP6XvvEkeSyUW2.articleMode_on.html|title=Spain Retains European Crown|publisher=eurobasket2011.com|access-date=September 18, 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket2011.com/en/coid_grVrtrKvGNcoMAgYHLOdl0.articleMode_on.html |title=Another Masterpiece For MVP 'La Bomba' |publisher=eurobasket2011.com |access-date=September 18, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120731172348/http://www.eurobasket2011.com/en/coid_grVrtrKvGNcoMAgYHLOdl0.articleMode_on.html |archive-date=July 31, 2012 }} Navarro won a silver medal with Spain at the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 London Summer Olympics]]. He also played at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2014 FIBA World Cup]], at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Rio Summer Olympics]], where he won a bronze medal, and at the [[2017 EuroBasket]], where he also won a bronze medal. ==Post-playing career== After Navarro retired from playing professional basketball, in August 2018, he began working in the front office of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] club [[FC Barcelona Basket|FC Barcelona]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/839760/juan-carlos-navarro-to-join-fc-barcelona-basketball-structure|title=Juan Carlos Navarro to join FC Barcelona Basketball structure|website=www.fcbarcelona.com}}[https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/juan-carlos-navarro-retires/ar-BBM4e9U It took Juan Carlos Navarro a long time to try the NBA.] In April 2021, Navarro was appointed as Barcelona's [[general manager (basketball)|general manager]], by the [[President (corporate title)|President]] of the club, [[Joan Laporta]]. Navarro replaced [[Ignacio Rodríguez (basketball)|Nacho Rodríguez]] in the role. On July 31, 2026, the club announced Navarro would be stepping away from his role as general manager to become an ambassador and player mentor for Barcelona's basketball section.{{cite web | title=Juan Carlos Navarro, new ambassador and mentor for the basketball team|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/4551030/juan-carlos-navarro-new-ambassador-and-mentor-for-the-basketball-team | website=fcbarcelona.com | date=31 July 2026 |
